diagnosis.root_cause: The ONU fibre path changed: measured distance stepped from 95 km to 41 km and remained there. After that path change, RX power progressively deteriorated from approximately -18 dBm to -26.58 dBm, indicating a changed or poorly repaired fibre route with increasing loss. The ONU remains online, while TX power, TX bias, supply voltage, OLT, router, VLAN, and RADIUS state are normal.
evidence: The ONU is online and responding, so this is not an ONU-offline or total service outage.
The 168-hour distance series is stable at 95 km, then makes a discrete step to 41 km and remains there; distance is expected to be constant, so this is direct evidence of a fibre-path change.
RX power subsequently worsens progressively from about -18 dBm to -26.6 dBm, currently in the degraded range, consistent with loss on the changed or poorly repaired path.
TX power remains normal around +2.4 dBm and TX bias current stays within the healthy 9.5-13.0 mA range, so laser degradation is not supported.
The eight visible peers on EPON0/5 are online with mostly normal RX levels, ruling against a PON-port-wide failure or splitter-wide impairment.
OLT health, CPU, memory, temperature, SNMP, and all tested PONs are normal; the router heartbeat and resource state are also normal.
Expected VLAN 1115 is present and RADIUS data matches CRM, so stuck provisioning, missing authentication, suspended service, and line-ID conflict are not indicated.
The customer has eight sessions in 24 hours with short durations, which is abnormal and likely a consequence of the deteriorating optical path rather than an authentication fault.

remediation.action: Dispatch fibre technicians to inspect the subscriber drop, splice closures, splitter path, and any recent repair or reroute. Verify the optical route and OTDR distance against the expected 95 km path, clean and reseat connectors, inspect for bends or damaged splices, and restore the correct path or repair the newly degraded section. Recheck RX power and distance after repair; investigate the ONU or replace it only if the optical path tests clean. Monitor session frequency after optical levels recover.

ground_truth.root_cause: A re-splice four days ago shortened the path from 95 m to 41 m and initially improved RX from -20.8 to -18.2 dBm. Since then RX has fallen steadily to -26.5 dBm, so the new splice itself is failing.
expected_reasoning: Current RX of -26.1 dBm is in the degraded band and live RX is worse still at -26.6
The recent RX series shows a clear downward slope, which alone reads as fibre degradation
Looking further back, distance stepped from 95 m to 41 m four days ago
At that same moment RX jumped upward from -20.8 to -18.2 dBm, consistent with a shorter path
So the sequence is: path shortened and improved first, then began degrading from the new baseline
The customer's statement that it was fixed last week corroborates a work visit at that point
TX power, bias current and supply voltage are flat, so the ONU is not implicated
Peers on EPON0/5 are normal, so the fault is in this customer's own path
A splice made four days ago that is now losing 8 dB is a defective splice, not coincidental degradation

expected_escalation.review_reason: Rework of a splice completed four days ago; the original job should be reviewed

distractors: The recent RX slope is a textbook fibre degradation signature
The distance step is buried three days back in the series
Eight sessions in 24h invites a flapping diagnosis
